notes: This is a single-channel SDI-to-fiber transmitter (TX only, 'FTX' = fiber TX), one of a matched TX/RX pair (receiver is the separate SB-12G-FRX-ST). BNC video connector supports multi-rate SDI from 5Mbps to 12Gbps (SMPTE 424M/292M/297M/2081-1/2082-1); graded sdi-12g as the top-rated bandwidth for this port per the connector's max supported standard. Fiber connector is physically an ST-type optical connector (metallic bayonet), not present in the allowed connector enum list -- mapped to 'fiber-lc' as the closest fiber category; no bandwidth grade applies to fiber ports per the grading rules given. Power input is a locking 4-pin mini-XLR (confirmed via Multidyne's own SilverBullet family literature and cross-referenced B&H/Markertek listings); mapped to 'xlr4-dc' as the closest connector id. Not rack-mountable (handheld/inline unit, ~3.2 x 0.65 x 0.75 in, ~4 oz including cable pigtail). Cross-verified across Markertek spec table, B&H Photo listing, and Multidyne's own SilverBullet-family datasheet/manual (note: Multidyne's current site now markets a newer 'SilverBullet 2' successor line, SB2-12G-TX-ST, with the same architecture -- BNC in / ST optical out / mini-XLR4 power -- used here only to corroborate connector types, not as the primary spec source for this exact SKU).

ports.name: Optical Out (ST)
ports.note: Physical connector is a metallic ST-type optical connector (singlemode fiber, 1310nm, -3dBm TX launch power). 'ST' is not in the allowed connector enum; fiber-lc chosen as closest fiber-optic analog.

ports.name: Power 5-16VDC In
ports.note: Locking 4-pin mini-XLR DC power input, 5-16VDC, ~1-1.5W. Powered via included AC adapter or optional D-Tap/USB-A/USB-C accessory cables.
